title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 10
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 10: the weapons that are not of the flesh, what some said about Paul's letters and his speech, and boasting in the Lord.

questions.text: How does Paul describe himself in their presence and when he is absent?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says that in their presence he is lowly among them, but being absent he is bold toward them.

answers.text: Bold when present, lowly when absent
Silent when present, silent when absent
Harsh both when present and when absent
Lowly among them when present, bold toward them when absent

questions.text: What does verse 3 say about how they wage war?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that though they walk in the flesh, they do not wage war according to the flesh.

answers.text: They do not walk in the flesh and do not wage war at all
Though they walk in the flesh, they do not wage war according to the flesh
They wage war according to the flesh when needed
They leave the war to the assemblies

questions.text: What are the weapons of their warfare mighty before God for?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says the weapons of their warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds.

answers.text: For the throwing down of strongholds
For the building of a temple
For the gathering of the collection
For the judging of the assemblies

questions.text: What does verse 5 say they bring into captivity?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 speaks of throwing down imaginations and every high thing exalted against the knowledge of God, and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ.

answers.text: Every adversary who opposes them
Every letter written against them
Every thought, to the obedience of Christ
Every unclean thing in the temple

questions.text: For what purpose did the Lord give the authority he speaks of in verse 8?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says the authority which the Lord gave was for building them up, and not for casting them down.

answers.text: For building them up, and not for casting them down
For judging those outside the assembly
For collecting the gift for the saints
For appointing apostles in every city

questions.text: What did people say about his letters and his bodily presence?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 reports them saying: His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised.

answers.text: That both his letters and his bodily presence were weak and despised
That his letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech is despised
That his letters were weak but his speech was powerful and strong
That he never wrote to them at all, but only sent others to speak

questions.text: What does verse 12 say about those who measure themselves by themselves?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.

answers.text: That they are approved by the Lord
That they are to be imitated
That they boast within proper limits
That they are without understanding

questions.text: According to verse 14, how far did they come, and with what?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says they do not stretch themselves too much, for they came even as far as to the Corinthians with the Good News of Christ.

answers.text: They came to Macedonia only, and sent letters on
They came as far as Jerusalem with the collection
They came even as far as to the Corinthians with the Good News of Christ
They came no further than Ephesus

questions.text: What quoted words about boasting does verse 17 give?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 says: But "he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord."

answers.text: He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord
Let all that you do be done in love
Evil companionships corrupt good morals
Now is the day of salvation

questions.text: Who is approved, according to verse 18?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 says it is not he who commends himself who is approved, but whom the Lord commends.

answers.text: The one who commends himself
The one whom the Lord commends
The one who writes the weightiest letters
The one who boasts beyond proper limits
